source.author: verg
source.text: Hinc pecudes, armenta, viros, genus omne ferarum, quemque sibi tenues nascentem arcessere vitas; scilicet huc reddi deinde ac resoluta referri omnia nec morti esse locum, sed viva volare sideris in numerum atque alto succedere caelo.
source.text_original: Hinc pecudes, armenta, viros, genus omne ferarum, / quemque sibi tenues nascentem arcessere vitas; / scilicet huc reddi deinde ac resoluta referri / omnia nec morti esse locum, sed viva volare / sideris in numerum atque alto succedere caelo.
source.text_english: From this come flocks, herds, men, and every kind of wild beast, each one to summon for itself the thin life at birth; plainly, to be returned here afterward and, once dissolved, brought back, and that there is no place for death, but that, alive, they fly into the rank of the stars and rise up into the lofty sky.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: ac ne quis forte ignoraret, quisnam esset ille spiritus qui tantum haberet potestatis, declarauit alio loco dicens: deum namque ire per omnis terrasque tractusque maris caelumque profundum; hinc pecudes armenta uiros genus omne ferarum, quemque sibi tenuis nascentem accersere uitas.
reuse.text_original: ac ne quis forte ignoraret, quisnam esset ille spiritus qui tantum haberet potestatis, declarauit alio loco dicens: deum namque ire per omnis terrasque tractusque maris caelumque profundum; hinc pecudes armenta uiros genus omne ferarum, quemque sibi tenuis nascentem accersere uitas.
reuse.text_english: And lest anyone perhaps be ignorant who that spirit was that had such great power, he explained elsewhere, saying: for God goes through all lands and the stretches of the sea and the deep sky; from him come flocks, herds, men, and every kind of wild beast, and he calls to himself each one as it is born for its brief life.
